source: Our analysis reveals a clear upward trend in the percentage of songs with a predominantly negative emotional sentiment, particularly since the mid-2010s.
claim: The yearly share of top-10 songs classified as predominantly negative averaged 22.1% in 1960-2014 and 39.1% in 2015-2020.
code: b.assign(year=pd.to_datetime(b.chart_week).dt.year).query('1960 <= year <= 2020 and peak_pos <= 10').groupby('year').Sentiment.apply(lambda s: s.eq('Negative').mean() * 100).groupby(lambda y: '2015-2020' if y >= 2015 else '1960-2014').mean().round(1)

source: Joy, while still the most common individual emotion, has been on a relative decline.
claim: Joy was the largest share of emotion words in the average top-10 song in every year from 1960 to 2020, falling from 28.3% in 1960 to 16.4% in 2020.

source: This rise in negativity is not attributable to any single emotion, but rather a confluence of increases in sadness, fear, disgust, and anger.
claim: In the average top-10 song, anger's share of emotion words rose from 5.1% in 1960 to 12.0% in 2020, disgust's from 4.6% to 8.3%, fear's from 8.0% to 15.5% and sadness's from 9.8% to 15.2%.

source: Taylor Swift, for example, started out with mostly positive, lovestruck anthems, but has increasingly explored darker, more introspective themes in her recent work.
claim: The share of Taylor Swift's top-10 songs classified as negative was 0% in the 2000s, 12.5% in the 2010s and 33.3% in 2020.
code: b.assign(year=pd.to_datetime(b.chart_week).dt.year).query("1960 <= year <= 2020 and peak_pos <= 10 and performer == 'Taylor Swift'").assign(decade=lambda x: x.year // 10 * 10).groupby('decade').Sentiment.apply(lambda s: s.eq('Negative').mean() * 100).round(1)
